verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. Lean's coefficient matrix for the same two blocks is the unfactored moment matrix `LocalizedMomentRepair.matrix a l u = fun i j => ∫ t, t ^ a i * bump (l j) (u j) t`. Its exponent rows are the paper's exactly (angularPowers λ = ![2, -2-2λ, -2λ]; axialPowers λ = ![1, 1-2λ]), but two things of the display are absent from it. (i) In the Lemma 8.7 pipeline the entries are never evaluated to μ_p e^{jdp}: the profiles there are bumps on pairwise disjoint cells of the patch rather than e^{jd}-dilates of one η_0, their moments stay as the integrals `FiveProfileMoments.bumpMoment` (:151), and nonsingularity comes from `PowerMomentMatrix.intervalMomentMatrix_det_ne_zero` (:216) rather than from the displayed factorisation. The factorisation is not missing from the repository, only from this matrix: for the two-row outgoing-pulse instance of the very same `LocalizedMomentRepair.matrix`, `OutgoingPulseBounds.actual_matrix_entry` (:565) evaluates the entries to μ_{p_i} e^{(p_i+1)c_j}, `normalizedMatrix_entry` (:582) puts row i in the displayed shape μ_{p_i}·(1, e^{d p_i}), and `normalizedMatrix_det_ne_zero` (:618) proves the determinant nonzero by μ_0μ_1(e^{2β_0} − e^{2β_1}) ≠ 0 — the paper's own argument of dividing the rows by μ_p and reading the Vandermonde in the distinct e^{dp}. That is a 2×2 instance with the pulse exponents −(1/2+λ), −(1/2+2λ), so it is not a counterpart of A_θ (3×3, powers 2, −2−2λ, −2λ) or A_z (2×2, powers 1, 1−2λ); the paper's method is formalised, for other rows. (ii) The row constants 1, 2a, -a and 1, a are not in the Lean matrix: they are divided into the target vector instead (angularDebt C d = ![0, -(d 0)/(2C), d 2/C], axialDebt C d = ![0, -(d 1)/C]), with the amplitude C of `background lam C R = C * R ^ (-1 - 2λ)` (FiveRowRank.lean:110) playing a(η) of (8.24). I checked these constants against the Lean rows themselves: pressure_row (line 189) gives 2C ∫ R^{-2-2λ}Δv = -d₀, angular_row (206) gives C ∫ R^{1-2λ}γ = -d₁, axial_row (223) gives -C ∫ R^{-2λ}Δv = -d₂, matching the 2a, a, -a of the display. Since A_θ = diag(1, 2a, -a)·M and A_z = diag(1, a)·M', the two parametrisations determine the same correction; what the repository does not contain is the explicit matrix as displayed. The nonsingularity the paper reads off the Vandermonde is proved for the Lean matrix at arbitrary distinct exponents (matrix_det_ne_zero), which covers the paper's exponents for λ > 0 (angularPowers_injective, FiveRowRank.lean:84). Hence low, not medium.

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Routine rewriting, in two steps. (1) Coefficients: Lean's `coefficients a l u b = M⁻¹.mulVec b` with M the moment matrix of the profiles and b = angularDebt / axialDebt. Because A_θ = diag(1, 2a, -a)·M and A_z = diag(1, a)·M' (row constants verified against FiveRowRank.pressure_row:189, angular_row:206, axial_row:223), A_θ⁻¹(0, -𝒫_q, -𝒥_{z,q})ᵀ = M⁻¹(0, -𝒫_q/(2a), 𝒥_{z,q}/a)ᵀ = M⁻¹·angularDebt, and A_z⁻¹(0, -𝒥_{θ,q})ᵀ = M'⁻¹·axialDebt — the Lean u_j and s_j are the display's, for Lean's own profile family. (2) Realization: ∑_j u_j η_j is `repair` (three summands for Δv via angularPowers, two for γ_d via axialPowers, matching j = 0,1,2 and j = 0,1), and the prefactor q^{-A} with argument r/√q is `scaleField ell U` at ell = √q, U = q^{-A}, instantiated exactly so in physical_rows_on_shaped_patch (MeanRankUpdate.lean:1153-1162). The q-subscripted targets correspond to `normalizeDebt ell U d` (line 33), which divides the physical debts by the matching ell/U powers before the inversion. Two caveats, neither a difference in this formula: the η_j are Lean's disjoint-cell bumps rather than the paper's e^{jd}-dilates, so the numerical u_j, s_j differ (recorded under eq-p097-3 and eq-p098-1); and the Lean fields are functions of r alone, the (z,t) dependence of Δv_phys entering through q and the amplitude as parameters of the chart point.

Rewriting: T_0(g_r − ρ𝒫) is `VariableGaugeMean.meanPressure = compactPrimitive ∘ pressureSource`, where `pressureSource f z = f z − density(z)·pressureMass f z.2.1` and `pressureMass f s = ∫ torusAverage f (r,s) dr`, i.e. exactly the paper's 𝒫 = ∫⟨g_r⟩_Y dR and p_m = T_0(g_r − ρ𝒫) of p. 108; `reconstructState` sets the state's pressure to that of its own g_r, and `cycle_reconstructed` says every stage of the actual cycle is reconstructed, so the mean pressure at stage j is T_0(g_r^{[j]} − ρ𝒫^{[j]}). `meanPressure_sub_on` then states T_0(f − g) = T_0 f − T_0 g; taking f = g_r^{[j]}, g = g_r^{[j−1]} and using linearity of `pressureMass` inside `pressureSource` gives p_m^{[j]} − p_m^{[j−1]} = T_0(g_r^{[j]} − g_r^{[j−1]} − ρ(𝒫^{[j]} − 𝒫^{[j−1]})), the mean part of (9.16). The Q^{2A} factor is the chart normalization: `pressureMeanStages` is `meanField … (2 * CoordinateAlgebra.A h) …` and `Atlas.physical_eq` gives physical = Q^{−degree} × normalized, so the physical increment times Q^{2A} is the normalized one. The wave part p_w^{[j]} − p_w^{[j−1]} is not inside this display at all: in Lean it is the two separate summands `particularPressure j + signedPressure j` of `positivePressure`. Differences that remain: Lean's linearity lemma carries ContDiffOn and SupportedGauge hypotheses and holds at points of a slow domain, where the paper asserts the identity outright 'in a fixed Q chart'; and the ρ-subtraction is built into the operator rather than written as a separate term.

verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. No declaration was found stating the paper's packaged physical bound |F^{[j]}|_m ≤ C_{j,m,N} q^N for the stage's flat remainder. What the Lean states instead, by another formula, is all-powers flatness of each constituent of `errors.total` in chart scales. `NativeBounds N U gain loss f` unfolds (PhysicalResidualJetBounds.lean:375-380) to smoothness plus: ∀m ∃A ≥ 0, ∃p, ∀ l n, N ≤ n → ∀ x ∈ U, ∀ j ≤ m, ‖∂^j f_{l,n}(x)‖ ≤ A · Q_n^{gain − loss(m)} · S_n^p. The three constituents are bounded for EVERY real α, but not with identical data: `baseError_native` (:371) gives gain h·α, loss `fun _ => 0`, on the lifted domain; `axis_native` (:168) gives gain h·α, loss `fun _ => 0`, on the unlifted `strip.domain`; `gaussian_field_native` (:833) carries an extra band hypothesis hN and a per-order loss `fun m => 2·h·m`, on the lifted domain. So the gaussian chart bound already loses 2·h·m derivatives-worth of gain at order m: its exponent is h·α − 2·h·m, not h·α. All-powers flatness at each fixed order survives — α is universally quantified, so for fixed m the quantity h·α − 2·h·m is still arbitrarily large — but that step has to be said rather than assumed. Conjoining the three is therefore not available at loss 0: `excluded_nativeBounds` (PhysicalResidualJetBounds.lean:1027) requires one common N, U, gain and loss, and the repository supplies them in `native_residual` (:861-872), which first lifts `axis_native` to the lifted domain and weakens all three to gain h·(1/2+σ) with the common loss `fun m => 2·h·m` before calling it. Three differences from (9.5) as written. (i) Scale: the Lean bound is a chart bound in Q_n^{h·α−loss} with ε_n^α = Q_n^{h·α} (ChartScales.epsilon h n = Q n ^ h), not a physical bound in q^N; the repository's chart-to-physical dictionary is `selected_residual_jet_bound`, and it is applied to the realized state's full residual, not to the flat remainder alone, and it converts at a further derivative loss (physicalLoss h β m) that the paper's statement does not carry. (ii) Constant: the Lean's right-hand side keeps a slow factor S_n^p, so the constant is uniform over labels and points but not literally over bands; uniformity in the paper's sense is recovered by absorbing S_n^p into a slightly smaller exponent, which the ∀α quantifier permits but which I did not verify as a repository lemma. (iii) Range: the Lean bounds hold for bands n ≥ 4, and on the lifted strip domain for the base error and the gaussian field but on the unlifted strip domain for the alias, where the paper states them outright and on one domain. Severity low rather than medium because the surrounding argument is still proved: the Lean's downstream use of these three bounds is exactly `native_residual`, which deliberately weakens all the flat terms to the single common gain h·(1/2+σ) and common loss 2·h·m, so the later argument never needs (9.5)'s arbitrary power.

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. No declaration defines a function D_{v,a}(m) indexed by a source vertex a, and nothing in the repository builds a DAG of the correction construction. The same bookkeeping is carried out twice, each time inside one inductive expression type rather than once for the whole construction. (i) GenericDifferentialPolynomial.Expression has nodes input / coeff / add / mul / directional — the paper's "sums, products, derivatives" — but no node for the "proved inverses" the paper also lists as graph operations, and no node of general weight d_{v,w}: a derivative node adds exactly one order, so an operation costing d derivatives is d stacked nodes. Its ApproximationRates.threshold : ℕ → ℕ propagates by the paper's recursion: directional gives threshold m = a.threshold (m+1) (the edge weight d_{v,w} = 1), add gives max of the two children at the same m (d_{v,w} = 0), a coeff node gives 0, matching the initial value D_{b,a}(m) = 0 for b ≠ a, and in polynomial_jetRate_of_stages the input nodes are given threshold = id, matching D_{a,a}(m) = m. mul takes sup over k ≤ m of each child's threshold rather than the child's value at m; every threshold built here (id, 0, max, m ↦ θ(m+1), and sup over k ≤ m) is monotone, so that sup equals the child's value at m and the two agree, the Lean version being the safe choice for a non-monotone threshold. Two things do differ from the display. The propagated quantity is literally the approximation-stage index J required for the tail estimate at jet order m (tail_rate : ∀ m J, threshold m ≤ J → …), not a count of derivatives of an input field; the two are identified only through the hypothesis htail (m ≤ J) of polynomial_jetRate_of_stages, which is what forces threshold = id at the sources. And one function is carried instead of one per source a: the maximum over sources is taken as the recursion proceeds, so what is computed is max_a D_{v,a}(m), the coarsening the paper's conclusion uses. (ii) FlatKernelBounds.Expr.jetOrder is the same recursion for the kernel expressions: k at a jet k source node, 0 at every non-source node, max over the children at add and mul; there the m + d_{v,w} shift is performed by rewriting the expression with Expr.diff, which sends jet k to jet (k+1), instead of by shifting the counting function's argument. Neither construction is applied to the correction-stage graph of Lemma 9.7. In that chain the finiteness of the derivative counts is not needed as a separate step, because every stage field is asserted smooth of infinite order (ActualCandidateAssembly.stages_smooth : ∀ j, ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (potentialStages …) (physicalDomain …), and likewise for directStages and pressureStages, lines 879-889) and the per-order estimates are stated with the derivative order m quantified in front of the constant (WholeDomainStageBounds.actual_finite_residual_bound). So the paper's formula as written was not checked; what was checked in its place is the same recursion for two restricted classes of expressions, plus infinite-order smoothness of the stage fields.

Both equalities are nevertheless a two-line rewriting of stated declarations. The hold is the plateau of `releaseSlope` (= -1 on [1, d.secondRampStart], with d.secondRampStart = 1 + d.longHold and d.longHold = 4 log(1/h)), so hold start = d.releaseStart + 1 and hold end = d.releaseStart + d.secondRampStart. Throughout the hold y - tailStart d ≤ -1 - decayHold d < 1 (tailStart d = d.releaseStart + d.rampEnd + decayHold d, d.rampEnd = d.secondRampStart + 1, decayHold_pos), so tailShape_early makes the tailShape factor in both formulas exactly 1 - d.rho and it cancels from the ratio. First equality: energyDensity_release_eq gives (XE^2)(hold end)/(XE^2)(hold start) = exp(2 (releasePrimitive(secondRampStart) - releasePrimitive(1))) = exp(-2 longHold) by the increment step contained at TailEnergyBounds.lean:82, = h^8 by plateau_suppression. Second equality: finalAngular_release_formula carries the extra similarity factor exp(-(y - releaseStart)/2), so E(hold end)/E(hold start) = exp(-longHold) * exp(-longHold/2) = h^4 * h^2 = h^6 by plateau_amplitude_suppression. Recorded as a fact and not a defect: downstream the repository does not use the exact h^6 ratio but the inequality finalAngular_suppressed, ≤ 2 E(releaseStart) h^4, measured from the release start rather than from the hold start; that is what TerminalCone.release_small and TerminalCone.profileAxialStress_le_angular consume.

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. A regrouping of the same identity, at the right layer of the construction. The paper fixes the angular moment first ('The angular moment is now fixed independently of the pulse amplitude. The remaining scalar condition is S(∞) = 0', p.132), so the S(∞) of (A.19) is computed with the moment-correction bumps already in place; the counterpart is therefore the corrected normalisation, not PulseAmplitude.totalEnergy_normalized, whose totalEnergy uses the pre-reset OutgoingTail.finalAngular. CorrectedPulseAmplitude.totalEnergy uses correctedAngular, i.e. E(1 + c₀bump₀ + c₁bump₁), the relative change the paper describes on p.132, and resetDensity_support puts its support in [releaseStart - 4, releaseStart], at the exterior-transition start. Left-hand sides then match term for term: lam * totalEnergy d c A eta / (normalization d.core * shape eta ^ 2) is λS(∞)/(X_p e_b² f²), with normalization = e^{pulseStart} pulseAmplitude² = X_p e_b² and shape eta = (1 + η²)⁻¹ = f(η). On the right the Lean writes an explicit quadratic in A rather than the paper's K_b A² - (1 - e^{-26})/4 + 𝓔. The identification is: quadraticCoefficient = pulseConstant + (a λ-small repair integral) by quadraticCoefficient_eq, where pulseConstant is literally ∫_0^13 e^{-2z} mainPulse(z)² dz = K_b (mainPulse is the Lean name for the paper's R_0, and the Lean bounds pulseConstant_upper ≤ 1/4, pulseConstant_lower > 1/5 match the paper's ≤ 1/4 and > .20); the corrected constantTerm is PulseAmplitude.constantTerm - energyShift, and PulseAmplitude.constantTerm contains the literal summand -RadialSchedule.pulseEnergyDebt = -(1 - e^{-26})/4; and the paper's error term is the remainder, 𝓔(A,η) = (quadraticCoefficient - pulseConstant) A² + linearTerm d.core eta * A + (constantTerm d c eta + pulseEnergyDebt), the last bracket being (constantCorrection + normalizedPrefixAxial) etaPolynomial² - normalizedPrefixAngular - normalizedTail - energyShift. The -energyShift summand is the normalised reset energy, λ·resetEnergy/(2 X_p e_b² f²), which is exactly the paper's remark that 'the exponentially small affine end bumps account for its remaining dependence'. With that reading the two displays are the same equation; the Lean never names 𝓔 and instead keeps its pieces separate, which is what lets the next display be stated coefficient by coefficient.

verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. No declaration assembles the display as written: the ρ^{-r} factor, the coefficients c_j(η) and the amplitude v_* are never brought together in one statement. The scaling factor itself — one inverse power of the width per derivative — IS in the repository, in one dimension and for exactly the base profile of the paper's β_j: SmoothCutoffs.scaledCutoff_iteratedDeriv states the all-order chain rule iteratedDeriv n (scaledCutoff a) = a^n · (iteratedDeriv n cutoff)(a·), and with cutoff_iteratedDeriv_bounded (|iteratedDeriv n cutoff| ≤ C) this gives ‖∂_X^r β(·/ρ)‖_∞ ≤ C_r ρ^{-r} on taking a = ρ⁻¹; scaledCutoff_iteratedDeriv_bound is the packaged form, |∂^{n+1} scaledCutoff a (q)| ≤ C (1/q)^{n+1}. The β_j are that same profile: LocalizedMomentRepair.bump l u t = cutoff((t-(l+u)/2)/((u-l)/4)) and FiveProfileMoments.bump P j = LocalizedMomentRepair.bump (lower P j) (upper P j), i.e. a translated dilate with ρ = (u-l)/4. (cutoff_iteratedFDeriv_le, ‖∂^n (baseCutoff(R⁻¹ x))‖ ≤ C_n / R^n, is the further R³ analogue for the localized-energy cutoff.) What the correction bounds do instead is absorb the width into the constant, because the Patch — hence ρ — is fixed before the constant is chosen: FiveProfileMoments.mixed_jet_bound has the same shape as the display (a bound, uniform in x, on the mixed jet ∂_η^m ∂_x^k of the bump combination by the m-th parameter jet of the coefficients, with the β_j independent of η exactly as in the paper) but its J = J(P,N) hides ρ; correction_derivative_bound is its parameter-free case, |∂_x^k Σ_j c_j β_j| ≤ C‖c‖ with C = C(P,k). Neither exhibits ρ^{-r}, and neither carries the amplitude v_*. For the concrete pulse corrections the Lean proves the log-coordinate analogue that the paper's next sentence anticipates: correctionJet is ∂_y^k of δV(e^y), i.e. (X∂_X)^k, bounded by C·exp(-1/(4λ))·(1+|amp η|) with C independent of λ (paper_correction_bounds) — the bumps there have fixed width in log X, so no ρ^{-r} arises — and only the first η-derivative is bounded (correctionJet_eta_bound), not all k. The amplitude enters as an additive factor (1 + |amp η|) rather than as the multiplicative v_*. Passing from the (X∂_X)^k bounds to the display's ∂_X^r ρ^{-r} form, and iterating η-derivatives past the first, is not carried out anywhere I found.

The I- and S-lines are in the HeatedOutgoing/radial-X strand, the Q_s/N_s lines in the OutgoingHistories/log-y strand. verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The paper's display says the radial average 𝒜_X is a contraction towards the constant-in-X comparison value U_*, in the C^k_η norm, uniformly for 0 < X ≤ X_i. Lean states this at k = 0 and k = 1 in one declaration: normalized_history_bounds takes sup-over-holdRegion hypotheses on U_r − U_* and on ∂_η U_r − ∂_η U_* (with U_* = NaturalAxisData.U j η, X-independent as in the paper, and ∂_η U_* = 4) and concludes the same bound for 𝒜_X U_r and for 𝒜_X(∂_η U_r), for every point of holdRegion = Icc 0 110 ×ˢ Icc (−1) 1, i.e. with the paper's sup over 0 < X ≤ X_i = 110 and over η already taken. Its engine is average_error_bound, which is the paper's inequality one scalar field at a time and pointwise in X: if |Λ(F(tX,η) − b)| ≤ B for all t ∈ [0,1] then |Λ(average F (X,η) − b)| ≤ B (Λ is a free positive scale; take Λ = 1). For k ≥ 2 the rewriting is: apply average_error_bound to F = ∂_η^k U_r and b = ∂_η^k U_*(η), move the k parameter derivatives through the average with parameterPartial_average, then take sup over X ∈ (0,X_i] and η ∈ [−1,1]; the right-hand side only grows because [0,X] ⊆ [0,X_i]. The one step Lean does not package is the iterated (k-fold) form of parameterPartial_average — only the single-order commutation is a lemma, though the analogous induction is carried out for `primitive` in ReferenceUniformJets.etaJet_primitive. Note the paper's C^k_η norm counts parameter derivatives only, which matches Lean's parameterPartial jets.

DIRECTION OF THE COMPARISON. The printed display bounds a norm, ‖log φ(X_i)‖ ≤ ‖log φ_* + log Φ(4,·)‖ + ½(M_k+.8)L_0, and a bound on a norm never yields a bound on a difference, which is what ReferenceEndpointRate.lean:203-204 states; so the display as printed neither implies nor is implied by the Lean statement. The paper's step in the increment form it is derived from is ‖log φ(X_i) − log φ_* − log Φ(4,·)‖_{C^k_η} ≤ (½M_k + .4)L_0, and that implies the Lean's (M+1)L_0 increment bound (with M = M_k, since ½M_k + .4 ≤ M_k + 1 for M_k ≥ 0), not conversely. The Lean constant is therefore strictly larger than the paper's for every M ≥ 0, and the Lean statement is the weaker one. verdicts.summary: Lean has a weaker form of it. The paper bounds all η-derivative orders of the stress-vector difference, Σ_{j=0}^m |∂_η^j(p_{s,N} - p_s)| ≤ C_m/N, for every m. What I found in Lean is the order-0 statement only: both profile_stocks_rate declarations bound |profileStockOne (P n) - profileStockOne Q| and |profileStockTwo (P n) - profileStockTwo Q| pointwise on the compact parameter set S, with no η-derivative of the difference bounded. (Lean's two stocks are the two components of the paper's p_s: profileStockOne = X·angularLag/L and profileStockTwo = X·axialLag/(L·E).) The Lean input is one η-derivative deeper than its output — profileData carries the row values together with their first parameterPartial, and profileHistory_first_jet_bound (ModulatedStockBounds.lean:283) feeds it a FiniteJetBound 1 — which matches the paper's own remark that order m of the stocks consumes order m+1 of the histories, at m = 0 only. Severity low rather than medium because I traced the paper's two uses of (C.16) in the proof of Proposition C.2 — preserving the cone inequality between the interval 𝒥 and the first correction interval, and preserving it inside the correction interval — and both are inequalities between stock values at a point, needing only j = 0. I did not find a higher-order η-jet rate for the stocks anywhere in the modulation files; the nearest higher-order statement, ActivationStocks.log_stocks_uniform_jets (:711), is about the activation ramp parameters (T, κ), not about the N-modulation, so it is not a counterpart.

verdicts.summary: Lean has a stronger form of it. The paper asserts moment equality at the single radius X_rep and field equality (Ẽ, Ũ) = (E, U) on X ≥ X_rep. Recorded here as stronger, not as a defect. One encoding note, verified: the structure field that literally carries this property, ModulatedProfileAssembly.Witness.restored (:443), is a projection and does not appear in the declaration index, so the indexed consequences rows_outside / fields_outside / exterior_pressure are cited in its place; I read the field at its source line.

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Same two inner products, differently normalised. The paper resolves the UNIT stress direction n = T_0/|T_0| against the shear frame (1, t_s), so both components carry the factor 1/|p_s - (a, -b_s)| (the F cancels). The Lean lemmas resolve the UN-normalised stress τ • (p_1 - a, p_2 - c) against the unit frame built from the shear vector, so both right-hand sides carry τ*F*a/‖F • (-a, -c)‖ instead; with s = (a, -b_s), c = -b_s, t_s = c/a, ‖F • (-a,-c)‖ = F|s| and a > 0 this is τ*a/|s|. Recovery: the F in the Lean right-hand sides belongs to the SHEAR vector F • (-a, -c), not to the stress, so the stress norm is ‖τ • (p_1 - a, p_2 - c)‖ = τ|p_s - s| with no F in it. Divide both Lean identities by τ|p_s - s| to get the components of the unit stress n against the unit frame: ⟪n, N⟫ = -(a/|s|)(P_c - v_s)/|p_s - s| and ⟪n, T⟫ = (a/|s|)J_c/|p_s - s|, where N = normalDirection(F•(-a,-c)) and T = transverseDirection(F•(-a,-c)). Then multiply by |s|/a = sqrt(1 + t_s^2), which is exactly the rescaling from the unit frame to the paper's unnormalised frame (1, t_s) — the paper's n_theta + t_s n_z is sqrt(1 + t_s^2) times the projection of n on the unit vector along (1, t_s) — and absorb the one sign (below). That gives the paper's n_theta + t_s n_z = (P_c - v_s)/|p_s - s| and n_z - t_s n_theta = J_c/|p_s - s|. Term by term the bracketed factors match the paper exactly: p_1 + p_2*(c/a) - a*(1 + (c/a)^2) = P_c - v_s and p_2 - p_1*(c/a) = J_c, with (4.20)'s P_c = p_{s,1} + t_s p_{s,2}, J_c = p_{s,2} - t_s p_{s,1}, v_s = a(1 + t_s^2). The overall minus sign in `stress_inner_normal` is the sign of `normalDirection` of the shear vector F•(-a,-c), which points opposite to (a, c); after that sign is absorbed the positivity clause '> 0' of the paper is the statement that P_c > v_s, which in Lean is carried separately as the `TargetCone.inward` field rather than inside this identity.

verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. What differs is the UNIFORMITY of kappa over the closed annulus, not the formula: the paper's two inequalities themselves, at kappa = 0, are carried pointwise by the Lean, in the paper's own quantities, over the whole open annulus. `FullTrueCone v` asserts `TrueConeLoop.InTrueCone p_1 p_2 A C` at every p with activeLeft W < p.1 < activeRight W and p.2 ∈ Icc (-1) 1 — the paper's range X_a < X < X_b, -1 ≤ eta ≤ 1. Unfolding `InTrueCone` with A = a, C = c, t_s = C/A, so that v_s = A(1 + (C/A)^2) = a(1 + t_s^2), P_c = p_1 + p_2 t_s and J_c = p_2 - p_1 t_s exactly as in (4.20), it gives 0 < a, 2 < v_s, 2 < P_c and v_s < coneBound P_c J_c; then `true_cone_iff` with hv : 2 < v_s turns the last two into v_s < P_c ∧ (v_s - 2) J_c^2 < 2 (P_c - v_s)^2. Dividing both by |p_s - (a, -b_s)|^2 > 0 and substituting the two identities of eq-p164-2 (n_theta + t_s n_z = (P_c - v_s)/|p_s - s| and n_z - t_s n_theta = J_c/|p_s - s|) gives n_theta + t_s n_z > 0 and (v_s - 2)(n_z - t_s n_theta)^2 < 2 (n_theta + t_s n_z)^2 — the paper's display at kappa = 0, with both inequalities strict. This is a proved statement for the constructed witness: `exists_weighted_profile` produces F, W, d, v with `FullTrueCone v` as its first conjunct. What is not stated anywhere found is a single kappa > 0 that makes both bounds uniform over the whole CLOSED annulus, which is what the paper's display asserts and what its later compactness use needs. The Lean obtains uniformity by two other routes instead. (a) `inner_direction_positive` and `outer_direction_positive` give a uniform margin eps for `directionProjection` and `directionGap`, but only on the two EDGE COLLARS, not on the whole range X_a < X < X_b; and there the margin is normalised against a different quantity. Writing the Lean direction as n = unitOfTilt t = (1, t)/sqrt(1 + t^2), so that n_theta = 1/sqrt(1 + t^2) and n_z = t/sqrt(1 + t^2), one has 1 + s t = (n_theta + s n_z)/n_theta and t - s = (n_z - s n_theta)/n_theta. Hence Lean's `eps ≤ directionProjection s t` reads n_theta + s n_z ≥ eps*n_theta, and Lean's `eps ≤ directionGap v s t` reads 2(n_theta + s n_z)^2 - (v - 2)(n_z - s n_theta)^2 ≥ eps*n_theta^2, whereas the paper's two inequalities are n_theta + t_s n_z ≥ kappa and 2(n_theta + t_s n_z)^2 - (v_s - 2)(n_z - t_s n_theta)^2 ≥ kappa*(n_theta + t_s n_z)^2. So both margins are proportional, but to powers of n_theta rather than to the constant kappa and to the projection respectively; the two are interconvertible only given bounds on n_theta, which these declarations do not carry. (b) On the CLOSED annulus the cone is additionally stated spectrally: `exists_closed_direction` gives a continuous unit direction field satisfying `ReferenceCone ∧ TargetCone` everywhere on Icc (-1) 1 ×ˢ Icc (leftEdge W) (rightEdge W), with `TargetCone` packaging inwardness (⟪T, normalDirection g⟫ < 0) and a strict ratio bound rather than an explicit kappa; `closed_shear_positive` supplies the accompanying a > 0, v_s > 2 on the closed rectangle. No declaration was found that states a single kappa ∈ (0, 2) satisfying both of the paper's inequalities simultaneously over the closed rectangle in the paper's normalisation; the uniform margin re-appears downstream only in the spectral variables. Per calibration rule 2 this is a uniformity/packaging difference, not a weaker mathematical statement of the formula itself: the formula holds pointwise at kappa = 0 by (FullTrueCone, InTrueCone, true_cone_iff) and the surrounding Proposition C.3 cone clause is still proved.
